Al Jazeera, Explainer, Business and Economy. LD datePublished = dateModified Thu 15 Oct 07:16 BST. By John Power.
Headline: 'G20 finance ministers, central bankers gather amid fallout from Iran war'.
RECONCILES AN APPARENT CONFLICT: the G20 finance ministers and central bank governors gather in Bangkok on Thursday, and 'The meetings are being held in conjunction with the annual meetings of the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the World Bank, taking place in the Thai capital from October 12 to October 18.' So the Guardian's 'IMF annual meeting in Bangkok' and the G20 meeting are the same venue and week, not rival claims.
G20 presidency currently held by the US. G20 countries account for about 85 percent of global GDP and three-quarters of global trade. Established 1999 after the Asian Financial Crisis.
Attending: most G20 finance ministers and central bank governors, plus IMF Managing Director Kristalina Georgieva and World Bank Group President Ajay Banga.
NOTABLE ABSENCE: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent will skip the gatherings despite the US holding the G20 chair; US officials cited 'domestic engagements'. Washington represented by Deputy Secretary Francis Brooke and Undersecretary for International Affairs Erin Browne.
Economic fallout from the US-Israel war on Iran expected to dominate. Disruption to shipping in the Strait of Hormuz has driven a surge in energy prices worldwide. Crude has exceeded $100 a barrel for much of the past eight months.
Jim Chalmers MP, Australia's Treasurer, in a statement ahead of the meeting: he would call for an end to the conflicts in the Middle East and the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz 'because that's what the global economy desperately needs'. 'The war in the Middle East is having a devastating economic impact and is pushing up fuel prices, inflation and interest rates around the world.'
Kristalina Georgieva, in a speech on Wednesday, warned mounting debt posed a threat to the global economy and that there was no 'magic' formula letting governments avoid tax rises or spending cuts. Debt exceeds 100 percent of GDP in the US, Canada, Japan, Italy and France.
Scott Bessent, in a statement addressed to the IMF on Wednesday, called for action on mismatched trade balances: 'This especially includes strengthening its analysis and engagement on the role non-market policies and practices and exchange rates play in driving external imbalances.' And: 'Policymakers around the world are having difficult discussions about how to sustain market-based systems amid distortionary policies from some economies that skew competition and hurt employment.'
China's cumulative trade surplus stood at $938bn in September.
At the last G20 finance ministers' meeting in Asheville, North Carolina on 31 Aug-1 Sep, members failed to issue a joint communique after China objected to trade language.
Next leaders' summit: Miami, Florida, 14-15 December.
BRITISH RELEVANCE: the UK is a G20 member; chancellor John Healey is in Bangkok (per Guardian business live) and was due to meet G20 finance ministers and central bankers and hold talks with Georgieva.
